items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Bishop and Eddy de Hass, who later changed his namee for Eddie O'Hare, arrived in Paris about the same time as I. We also had engaged a male singer this time... Bishop and Tommy were buddies who had gone to school together in Chicago.

ctx.x: We finished the 26th of April at the Cinema Rex and went to an engagement in Blankenberge, Belgium. Blankenberge is a summer resort on the North Sea and we opened at the Cave du Majestic on the beach, which is very early date to start a summer season and as it was so early, not many places that do business from June till September were open and we only worked the last three days of every week during that time until June.

Bishop received an offer from Switzerland to join an orchestra that was going into the Chikito, which paid him moremoney than he was making, working only weekends, so he left the 20th of May, and I came to Paris to look for another drummer. Fred Palmer left and went back to Italy, so I had to look for a tenor man also. After two days in Paris, I found a drummer who was a West Indian, whom everyone that knew him called "Dreamer". The tenor man I engaged was a Martinique named Andre Siobud. He was a good musician…

The owner of the Cave du Majestic had another place called the Palais d'Eté, not far from the Cave, which resembled a large beer hall. In fact they served more beer than any other drink. Alchohol is not served in most cafes and dance halls in Belgium. This place had two bandstands and engaged attractions. We had to play afternoon tea dances and I disliked that, because we had to play on a bandstand that was in the window near the entrance.
